Updated 4 September 2026. The user accepts the faster Engine implementation
for this experimental revision, including the separate regression documented
below. This is not a claim that every Engine test passes or that performance
is optimal. No manuscript source or environment was modified.

## Manuscript results first

The completed seven-case temperature and capture figures, source observations,
numerical checks, captions, and integration guidance are in
[the figure handoff](../../../figures/reactive_parallel/README.md).
All seven cases converged; capture mean absolute error is 5.85483 percentage
points. The substantial 6C/7C discrepancies remain visible.
These results use reactive nine-species bulk equilibrium, conventional
enhancement-factor transport, and empirical energy closure—not a resolved
reactive film, eNRTL comparison, or exact axial energy-conservation demonstration.
The cases do not need repeating solely to obtain a runtime example.

## Measured runtime

Three sequential fresh-start runs used the normal optimized wheel with no
call observers or temporary native tracing.

| Run | BVP wall (s) | BVP CPU (s) | Initialization, calculation and profiles (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| optimized_plain_1 | 34.8856 | 34.6506 | 51.7262 |
| optimized_plain_2 | 34.6569 | 34.5428 | 51.2601 |
| optimized_plain_3 | 34.4052 | 34.2316 | 51.4535 |

Median BVP time is **34.66 s**, range **34.41–34.89 s**. Median whole calculation
time is **51.45 s**, range **51.26–51.73 s**. Relative to the first-pass normal
wheel's measured 208.756 s BVP, this is approximately **6.02 times faster**
(83.4% less elapsed time). This is a comparison of measured configurations on
a shared desktop, not a theoretical optimum or an isolated hardware benchmark.
Peak process RSS across these runs is 203.51–207.86 MiB.

All three predict **91.54328696744% capture**. Against the first-pass result,
the maximum temperature-profile difference is 5.24e-11 K and the largest
difference across all 18 exported numerical tables, scaled by
max(1, |reference value|), is 6.39e-10, below the retained 1e-8 criterion.
The same 21-to-22-node mesh and two adaptive cycles are retained, with
maximum RMS residual 0.125340382574, zero scaled boundary residual,
physical boundary norm approximately 1.83e-14, and no domain guards or invalid
states. These checks establish numerical agreement, not independent physical
validity or mesh convergence.

A subsequent rebuild restoring the accepted experimental implementation has
a different wheel identity. Its fresh-start confirmation is retained separately
under `accepted_experimental_plain/`: **35.7818 s BVP**, **52.8563 s whole
calculation**, with the same capture, residuals, and mesh and no source changes.
The three timings above belong to the
identified measured wheel and are not silently relabeled as rebuild timings.

## Conditions and timing definition

Case 3C uses the adopted manuscript parameter set, neutral-vapor ePC-SAFT,
conventional enhancement-factor transport, and empirical energy relations.
The supplied column RHS Jacobian combines native thermodynamic derivatives
with derivatives of column algebra. Each process starts with a fresh
ideal-Henry initialization, not a previously solved reactive profile.

Settings: 21 initial nodes, tolerance 0.5, boundary tolerance 0.001, maximum
1000 nodes, explicit temperature states, raw state coordinates, reported dry
gas mass flow, and exact state reuse. These are deliberately coarse column
settings and must accompany any runtime claim.

Hardware: AMD Ryzen 5 5500, six physical cores/twelve logical CPUs, approximately
32 GB RAM, Linux; Python 3.13, NumPy 2.4.4, SciPy 1.17.1, pandas 3.0.2.
BLAS/OpenMP/MKL each use one thread. The existing CPU governor and other users'
processes were not changed. Runs were sequential on a shared desktop.

Installed package files are verified against the wheel ZIP. Source, input,
parameter, and wheel identities are recorded before each run and source files
checked again afterward. Imports, environment preparation, input-file loading,
and diagnostic-trace serialization are outside the timer. Fresh initialization,
column execution, both phases' profile calculation, and profile CSV serialization
are inside the whole-calculation timer. Peak RSS includes imported libraries.

## What was actually accelerated

The Engine now avoids unnecessary derivative calculations while retaining
the governing equations and consumed derivative outputs:

1. Exact primal-point phase reuse avoids repeated multiplier-independent EOS
   evaluations inside IPOPT; multiplier changes recombine the required Hessian
   algebra. Final certification remains fresh.
2. Ordinary finite-phase source-reference conversion requests the first
   temperature derivatives it consumes; explicitly requested higher-order
   calculations retain their own complete derivatives.
3. General-property evaluation computes the required exact temperature/density
   Hessian actions instead of an unused full reduced Hessian.
4. Pressure-root search and polishing use pressure and its density slope,
   including implicit association. The accepted root still receives complete
   properties and certification.
5. Density linearization reuses the association owner's exact site Jacobian.
   Phase blocks use exact Lagrangian Hessian actions along physical directions
   instead of unnecessary independent association-site columns.

No thermodynamic parameters, root bounds, polishing stencil, stability
criteria, or numerical acceptance tolerances were relaxed. Finite differences
in the new pressure-closure test are independent validation, not runtime
derivative approximations. The retained 18-request thermodynamic replay has
522 values and 2,610 Jacobian entries; maximum scaled differences from baseline
are 3.23e-12 and 3.35e-9 respectively, with unchanged optimizer iteration counts
and acceptable equilibrium certificates.

## Complete measured time accounting

The separately instrumented fast implementation recorded **8,097,579 nested
native spans**. Exclusive native regions plus exclusive Python/remaining
regions partition the measured experiment exactly in integer nanoseconds.
Inclusive nested times must not be added together.

| Stage | Total (s) | Native (s) | Python and remaining work (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Initialization | 7.026249 | 0 | 7.026249 |
| BVP | 35.576482 | 32.979377 | 2.597105 |
| Profile calculation | 9.638970 | 8.963653 | 0.675317 |
| Other setup/serialization | 0.115591 | 0 | 0.115591 |
| Whole experiment | 52.357292 | 41.943030 | 10.414262 |

The largest exclusive native BVP costs were phase Hessian actions (4.822 s),
IPOPT algorithm/internal linear algebra outside callbacks (4.020 s),
density Jacobian assembly (3.843 s), density recording/other work (3.670 s),
density Hessian actions (2.762 s), dispersion (2.643 s), and phase Jacobian
assembly (2.002 s). The BVP made 300,019 pressure/density evaluations,
8,659 complete state evaluations, and 561 equilibrium calculations.
The remaining costs and exact counts are retained in
[the native cost table](contracted_full_trace/native_stage_costs.csv),
[the Python cost table](contracted_full_trace/python_stage_costs.csv), and
[the accounting checks](contracted_full_trace/time_accounting.json).
Raw spans are retained as `contracted_full_trace/native_trace.npz`.
No runtime plot is needed.

This is an unsampled trace of named regions, not every machine instruction.
Internal IPOPT library functions remain aggregated; the region named
`equilibrium.kkt_sensitivities` specifically surrounds `populate_kkt_partials`,
not the complete sensitivity calculation. Instrumented times identify costs;
the normal-wheel timings above are the runtime result. There is no unexplained
multi-second file-writing sink, but further optimization remains possible.

## Accepted experimental regression and next work

The fastest implementation passed the affected **114-test gate**, plus native
architecture, lint, and typing checks. Running the four additional slow tests
produced **three passes and one failure**, specifically
`test_solved_temperature_boundaries_certify_bubble_dew_and_total_derivatives`.
The failing vapor-reference center reaches the fixed-pressure temperature
iteration limit. The liquid center and both parameter perturbations on each
side pass. This is separate from the demonstrated Case 3C calculation.

Controlled wheel comparisons isolate this regression to the phase-Hessian
action variant: retaining the other optimizations but reverting that contraction
passes all 118 tests. The fastest contraction was subsequently restored at the
user's explicit direction. The failure is retained and disclosed, not waived
as a passing test or hidden by changing tolerances.

The temperature-boundary probe stagnates at 296.7724020931804 K, with a pressure
residual of -6.03e-7 Pa against the 1.2e-7 Pa outer target; none of the sixteen
tested neighboring representable temperatures meets that target. The nested
fixed-temperature solver's pressure accuracy guarantee is looser than the
outer temperature solver demands. This provides a concrete next diagnostic
target: make nested accuracy consistent with the outer solve and verify its
derivatives and termination, rather than merely increasing iteration limits.
It does not prove that every failure of this type has the same cause.

Further performance work should use the retained exclusive-cost evidence.
Arbitrary cross-state tape reuse is not yet justified because the electrolyte
finite-size expression changes its series branch with reference density.
Any reuse must preserve those branches, derivative demands, and certification.
No statement that all performance problems have been eliminated is supported.

## Reviewer-ready runtime statement

For the nine-species reactive ePC-SAFT Case 3C column with conventional
enhancement-factor transport, three sequential runs of the optimized Engine
required a median 34.66 s BVP wall time (34.41–34.89 s) on an AMD Ryzen 5 5500
using single-thread numerical libraries. Including fresh Henry initialization
and profile generation increased the median calculation time to 51.45 s.
The mesh increased from 21 to 22 nodes at tolerance 0.5 and boundary tolerance
0.001. These are scoped, coarse-mesh single-case measurements, not a general
accuracy-matched ranking of numerical methods.
